picture: The parent is isostatically jammed with ~1080 pairs tied within 1e-12, one zero-contact rattler and uneven 5-15 degrees with a clear gap, so only topology-changing cluster surgery can escape the LP vertex.

diagnosis: Progress has stalled because the incumbent is a soft, marginally jammed configuration rather than a sharply resolved local optimum: only about five pairs lie below the $10^{-9}$ contact threshold, involving eight points and leaving 211 nominal rattlers, yet roughly $1{,}080$ pairs form a plateau at slack $10^{-8}$--$2\times10^{-8}$ before the slack jumps sharply. That plateau count matches the $219\cdot5-15=1{,}080$ tangent degrees of freedom, signalling a near-isostatic shell that conventional LP polishing, which selects constraints at $10^{-9}$, mostly fails to see. Consequently L-BFGS and LP steps merely equalise this shell and recover improvements of order its width, while deleting a few rattlers or hubs and reinserting them locally restores essentially the same near-contact topology. The missing structural property is an exactly active, rigid contact network with a certifying positive equilibrium stress, together with a genuinely different contact-graph basin rather than another perturbation of the published record.
